Definition: Beth-Peor, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Peor means house of Peor, and it is the landmark of the end of Moses' life. Israel abode in the valley over against Beth-peor in Deuteronomy 3:29, and Moses rehearsed the law there in Deuteronomy 4:46. Then Deuteronomy 34:6 says God buried Moses in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor, and no man knows his sepulchre to this day.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Beth-peor is holy ground because of what happened across the valley from it: the law given, and the lawgiver buried by God's own hand.
